summary: ITER-80 signup/onboarding/settings carryover pass — 5 of 7 features PASS, 2 CRITICAL bugs found in the mobile-carryover chain, plus 1 minor participant-path regression. Verified end-to-end via live UI + backend probes: (1) new `signup-cr-last-name` input renders, toggles hide/show correctly with role; (2) fresh caregiver signup persists care_recipient.first_name+last_name+relationship to /api/persona; (3) Onboarding StepEssentials prefills first_name='Louisa' + last_name='Davids' (verified visually — override to 'Emily' also works, confirming editable); (4) StepRecommended prefills onboarding-relationship='daughter' correctly; (5) Backend model change (CareRecipient.last_name Optional max_length=80) works — PUT validates 81 chars → 422, optional field roundtrips; (6) Persona regression suite 35/36 (30 persona + 5 new iter-80 tests + 1 known /auth/me mobile FAIL that IS the bug). CRITICAL BUGS: (A) StepRecommended `onboarding-caregiver-phone` prefill is EMPTY — expected '+61412345678' — because /api/account response contains only {summary, participants, members, addons, is_owner} (no `mobile`, no `owner.mobile`) AND /api/auth/me UserPublic model strips `mobile` field (mobile IS in DB, confirmed via mongo — just not surfaced). (B) Settings /settings profile-phone-input is EMPTY for the same root cause — fallback path `user?.phone_e164 || user?.mobile` never resolves because UserPublic returns neither. MINOR: routes/persona.py line 96-104 participant branch rebuilds CareRecipient using only first_name from user doc — drops last_name (verified: PUT with last_name='Selfcare' on participant → GET returns last_name=null).

critical.issue: UserPublic in backend/models.py:42 does not expose `mobile` (stored on users doc) or `phone_e164`. Blocks BOTH StepRecommended caregiver_phone prefill AND Settings /profile phone fallback. Frontend code (Onboarding.jsx line 88, Settings.jsx lines 202/208) reads user.mobile / user.phone_e164 — both are undefined for signed-up users.

Response omits account holder's mobile at both top-level and owner level. `_account_summary` in batch3_routes.py:171 returns {account_id, base_plan, ...} but no mobile. Onboarding.jsx line 88 reads `acct.mobile || acct.owner?.mobile` — both undefined.

minor.issue: routes/persona.py lines 96-104: when viewer_persona=='participant', backend rebuilds CareRecipient from user doc using ONLY first_name — drops last_name from the payload. Repro: PUT {care_recipient:{is_self:true,first_name:'Prue',last_name:'Selfcare'}} → GET returns care_recipient.last_name=null. Should mirror user.last_name / name split alongside first_name.

ui_bugs.issue: `onboarding-caregiver-phone` renders empty after signup with mobile='+61412345678'. Prefill effect at lines 72-106 reads acct.mobile || acct.owner?.mobile || user?.mobile — none exist in API responses. Fix requires backend exposing mobile on /api/account or /auth/me.

profile-phone-input renders empty for a user who signed up with mobile='+61412345678'. Fallback chain `user?.phone_e164 || user?.mobile` never resolves because UserPublic model doesn't expose either field. Feature described in review request #5 is NOT lit up in preview env.

integration_issues.flow: Signup mobile → Onboarding caregiver_phone prefill → Settings profile phone fallback
integration_issues.issue: End-to-end chain broken at the /api/auth/me + /api/account boundary — mobile IS persisted to Mongo (verified: db.users.findOne shows mobile:'+61412345678') but never surfaced back to the frontend. Frontend logic is correct; backend serializers need to include the field.

action_items: [HIGH] Add `mobile: Optional[str] = None` to UserPublic in /app/backend/models.py:42 (mobile is already stored on users doc; just not exposed). This single change fixes both the Onboarding caregiver_phone prefill AND the Settings /profile phone fallback simultaneously.
[HIGH-alt] OR: add `mobile: user.mobile` to the /api/account response in /app/backend/batch3_routes.py:_account_summary (Onboarding.jsx already reads acct.mobile).

[MEDIUM] Fix routes/persona.py:99-104 participant-branch — mirror last_name from user doc (e.g. `last_name = doc.get('last_name') or ((doc.get('name') or '').split(' ',1)[1] if ' ' in (doc.get('name') or '') else None)`). Otherwise the last_name captured on signup is silently dropped for participants (caregiver path is fine).
[LOW] Consider adding a data-testid on the /settings Profile tab button — Settings.jsx exposes phone input testid but not the tab-switcher for automated navigation.
critical_code_review_comments: UserPublic model has NEVER exposed mobile/phone_e164 (checked model definition line 42-59) — this Feb 2026 UX carryover work assumed the field would be available on `user` from useAuth(), but that assumption doesn't hold. Recommend a smoke test that hits the full carryover chain end-to-end in CI.

Onboarding.jsx line 88 defensively reads three fallbacks (acct.mobile || acct.owner?.mobile || user?.mobile) — good defensive coding, but ALL THREE resolve to undefined in the current backend. The 'defensive' pattern hides the missing-endpoint issue silently since the prefill effect swallows all errors — worth adding a one-time console.debug when carryMobile is falsy but user email exists.

routes/persona.py participant-mirror block silently DROPS non-first_name fields from the client payload — this is surprising API behaviour. If the participant branch must own the care_recipient shape, at minimum it should mirror ALL name-shaped fields (first + last) from the user doc, not just first_name. A comment explaining the truncation semantics would help.

backend/models.py:42 UserPublic uses ConfigDict(extra='ignore') — this means any field added to the mongo doc that isn't declared here is silently stripped from every /auth/me response. That's the root cause here, and it's a repeat pattern from previous iterations (see iter 76 persona_v1 fields also had to be plumbed through). Consider a shared 'ExposedFields' constant.

context_for_next_testing_agent: This iteration exposed a TWO-LAYER gap in the Feb 2026 signup carryover feature: backend model UserPublic + /api/account response both strip the `mobile` field that the frontend needs. The mobile IS persisted to mongo (verified). E1 needs to make ONE tiny model change (add `mobile: Optional[str] = None` to UserPublic in models.py:42) OR expose mobile in /api/account response. After the fix, retest: (a) StepRecommended `onboarding-caregiver-phone` should pre-fill; (b) Settings /profile phone should pre-fill. Also worth retesting after fixing the participant-path last_name mirroring in routes/persona.py:99-104. Test file `/app/backend/tests/test_iter80_signup_carryover.py` will be a good regression check — the `test_auth_me_returns_mobile` case is failing today and will pass once the UserPublic model exposes mobile.
rca of the issue: Root cause is a serializer-strip regression that's older than the Feb 2026 UX work — UserPublic in models.py has never included `mobile` even though the field is stored on user docs. The Feb 2026 carryover feature (Onboarding.jsx line 88, Settings.jsx line 202/208) was designed against the assumption that `user.mobile` or `user.phone_e164` would resolve from useAuth() — but AuthContext's setUser is fed from /auth/me → UserPublic response → `extra='ignore'` strips the field. Same pattern in /api/account (batch3_routes.py:_account_summary) which returns only summary/participants/members/addons/is_owner. FIX: (a) add `mobile: Optional[str] = None` to UserPublic (1-line), OR (b) inject `mobile: acct.get('owner_mobile')` into /api/account response (2 lines). Frontend needs zero changes — the fallback chain is already coded correctly and will just start resolving once backend exposes the value. Separately, routes/persona.py:99-104 rebuilds CareRecipient on participant PUT dropping last_name — a smaller bug from the Feb 2026 last_name addition that only affects the participant path.
